concept.name: Airdrop
concept.definition: An airdrop is the free distribution of tokens to a set of wallet addresses, typically to reward past users, bootstrap a community, or decentralize governance ownership, with eligibility usually set by an on-chain snapshot.
concept.intuition: It is a retroactive thank-you payment and marketing campaign in one: wake up, check your wallet, and there are tokens because you used the protocol before a cutoff date.
concept.mechanics: The project snapshots eligible addresses and activity, then makes tokens claimable (users pay gas to claim) or sends them directly. Uniswap's September 2020 UNI airdrop gave 400 UNI to each of 251,534 historical user addresses (10.06% of supply) plus pro-rata allocations to LPs. Airdrops are often paired with vesting for insiders while community allocations vest immediately.
concept.failure_modes: Sybil farmers create thousands of wallets to harvest eligibility, diluting genuine users; unexpected random airdrops are frequently dusting or scam tokens whose approval transactions drain wallets; large immediate floats can crash the token at listing.
concept.misconceptions: Airdrops are not free money in aggregate — their value comes from dilution and future expectations, and 'connect your wallet to claim' sites are the most common phishing lure. Airdropped tokens may be taxable income at receipt in many jurisdictions.
concept.example: In September 2020, every address that had ever called Uniswap v1 or v2 could claim 400 UNI (worth ~$1,200 at launch); even ~12,000 addresses whose transactions had only ever failed were included.
